metadata.title: BJP-IPFT-TIPRA Motha ने ट्राइबल का भरोसा तोड़ा | BJP-IPFt -TIPRA betrayed tribal trust in Tripura
metadata.description:
In the upcoming Lok Sabha Election 2024, the first phase of voting is scheduled for tomorrow, April 19. Tripura, a northeastern state with a substantial tribal population of around 34%, holds significance as 47 of the total seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes. The state has two parliamentary seats, where political alliances are shaping up for a competitive contest.

On one hand, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has aligned itself with two tribal parties, the Indigenous People's Front of Tripura (IPFT) and Tipra Motha, to consolidate support from the tribal community. Meanwhile, the Congress and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) are joining forces under the banner of the INDIA alliance to challenge the ruling BJP.

In this context, Kumud Debbarma, the secretary of the Tribal Youth Federation affiliated with the Communist Party of India (Marxist), provides a crucial perspective. His insights into tribal politics and the aspirations of the tribal youth in Tripura shed light on the complex dynamics at play in the upcoming election.

The election outcome in Tripura will not only influence the representation of tribal communities in the Lok Sabha but also determine the political landscape in the state and its implications for broader national politics.
